guides.wedding-video-editor.title: Edit a Wedding Video: Cuts, Music and Export Settings
guides.wedding-video-editor.desc: A practical wedding video editing workflow: assemble a rough cut, match music to the arc, and export in the right format for each channel.
guides.wedding-video-editor.lead: Edit to the emotional arc, not the chronology. A three-minute film that opens on a vow and closes on the dance floor beats a strict timeline.
guides.wedding-video-editor.f1v: Three to five minutes suits a highlight film
guides.wedding-video-editor.f2v: Keep most shots 2–5 seconds; hold a speech or vow longer
guides.wedding-video-editor.f3v: Clean ceremony audio carries the whole film
guides.wedding-video-editor.f4v: 1080p H.264 MP4, AAC audio, 16:9 unless vertical is required
guides.wedding-video-editor.s1: Build three passes: select the clips, assemble to music, then fix sound and colour. Lay down the best audio first — vows, a reading, a speech — and cut pictures over it. Keep transitions simple; straight cuts and a few dissolves age far better than effects. Finish with a colour pass so indoor and outdoor footage sit together, and always watch the whole film once at normal speed before exporting.
guides.wedding-video-editor.s2: Music licensing differs sharply by use: a track cleared for a personal wedding video is not automatically cleared for a photographer's portfolio or a paid advertisement, and platform detection varies by country. If the film will be posted publicly, use a licensed library track. Frame rate also depends on region — 24 or 25 fps is common where PAL traditions apply, 30 or 60 fps in North America — so match the source footage rather than forcing a conversion.
guides.wedding-video-editor.s3: Do not export a single master for every channel: a vertical social cut needs its own reframing, and a large ProRes master is useless to relatives on a phone. Avoid heavy noise reduction on low-light reception footage, which turns faces waxy. Back up the project file and the source media together, and keep the audio stems separate so a music change does not mean a full re-edit.
guides.wedding-video-editor.q1: How long should a wedding highlight film be?
guides.wedding-video-editor.a1: Three to five minutes is the usual sweet spot. A separate full-ceremony edit can be much longer and serves a different purpose.
guides.wedding-video-editor.q2: What export settings should I use?
guides.wedding-video-editor.a2: H.264 MP4 at 1080p with AAC audio is the most compatible default. Make a separate vertical 1080 × 1920 cut for stories and reels.
guides.wedding-video-editor.q3: Can I use a popular song?
guides.wedding-video-editor.a3: For a private film, often practically yes, but public posting can trigger muting or removal. Use a licensed track for anything shared publicly or commercially.
